#1998 REBASED ONTO POST-#2046 MAIN — 698dd77c7c. The predicted conflict
happened, and the resolution is cleaner than expected: MY REGENERATION COMMIT
WAS DROPPED, because #2046 made it obsolete.

    27e722785c  docs(architecture): regenerate the classifier inventory
                1 file, 1 line — a single drifted line number

After #2046 the inventory has NO line numbers, so that commit's entire content
is meaningless. `git rebase --skip` is the correct resolution rather than
resolving a conflict in it. I verified it contained nothing else first.

WHAT SURVIVED, checked rather than assumed:
    d046448c4e  the actual BUG-1286 change
    698dd77c7c  the monitor contract declaration
    SpecCompleted: True | RunCompleted: True  in events-follow.json
    inventory rows carrying :LINE            0
    --check                                  rc=0
    monitor contract                         12 surfaces verified
    aida-cli-lib --lib                       5200 passed, 0 failed

THIS IS THE CONVERGENCE ARGUMENT COMPLETING ITSELF. Three hours ago you argued
hand-regeneration does not converge. Two hours ago I produced an instance where
my manual fix CONFLICTED with the structural fix. Now the structural fix has
landed and the manual fix has been GARBAGE COLLECTED by a rebase — the conflict
resolved by deleting the workaround, not by merging it. That is what convergence
looks like from the other side, and #1989 should resolve the same way.

#1998's Build had already passed at 12m32s before the rebase, with the
monitor-contract fix in — so its suite is green on substance. This push restarts
CI on the rebased head.

NOT TOUCHING #1989. Same resolution applies to it, but it is not assigned to me
and it also carries a live F1 that needs a commit, not a rebase.
subject: #1998 rebased (698dd77c7c) — my regeneration commit was DROPPED as obsolete; the convergence argument completing itself
